lesson: A "pure tensor" test on period arrays needs scale-invariant inputs and quadruples matched by local similarity class, not isometry class. Fixed-n theta coefficient arrays are Siegel products yet fail the 2 x 2 identity, so "class numbers are not multiplicative" was the wrong reason for the Eisenstein row. The cusp computation was reachable without downloads: Hejhal data to primes below 3000 plus an invariance-validated GL(3) expansion; the largest m2 used was 167.
